personas.background: Runs evening workshops at a community arts centre and works part-time at a photography gallery. Has been the informal anchor of the collective for three years — organises the group calendar, books darkroom slots, and is the first contact for new members. Shoots medium format almost exclusively.

food.value: always eats before darkroom sessions and brings shared snacks unprompted — dislikes shooting on an empty stomach

activities.value: prefers methodical, unhurried darkroom sessions — gets visibly tense when members rush or skip fixing times

social.value: prefers small critique groups of 3–4 over full group showings, finds large group critique unfocused

domain_specific.value: strongly gravitates toward medium format — gently steers planning discussions toward 120 film shoots

preference_history.old_value: dismissive of lo-fi and toy camera aesthetics — sees them as technically undisciplined
preference_history.new_value: accepts lo-fi work as a legitimate approach when used with intention
preference_history.trigger: Sol's lo-fi pinhole series received strong outside-group praise; Nora acknowledged during the critique that the work had more intent than she had assumed

speaking_quirks: uses 'technically speaking' before any gear or process correction
ends organisational messages with the date and time bolded as a plain string ('next session: Saturday the 22nd, 10am')
responds to praise about her own work with a self-deprecating qualifier ('still not happy with the shadows on that one')

personas.background: Started shooting film 18 months ago after a disposable camera phase. Was brought in by Nora after showing up to an open workshop. Very active in the chat — shares references, asks questions, hypes others. Aspires to shoot medium format but is still building skills on 35mm.

food.value: always brings coffee drinks to sessions for the group — has never arrived empty-handed

activities.value: strongly prefers experimentation over technical precision — will shoot expired film, try random developers, double expose deliberately

social.value: messages between sessions daily — shares found images, references, and process shots constantly

domain_specific.value: treats camera gear aspirationally — constantly researching her next upgrade, currently fixated on medium format

preference_history.old_value: uses disposable cameras and cheap toy cameras almost exclusively
preference_history.new_value: committed to a fixed-lens 35mm camera as primary tool
preference_history.trigger: Nora lent her a Canonet for a session and the resulting roll was the best she had produced — she bought her own the following week

speaking_quirks: starts reaction messages with 'okay but' before the compliment ('okay but this shot is EVERYTHING')
uses 'low-key' as a modifier to soften strong opinions ('low-key think this is your best roll ever')
asks questions in clusters — three in one message rather than one at a time

personas.background: Has been shooting film for 22 years. Was a founding member of the collective. Technically rigorous, slightly conservative about methodology — sceptical of anything that looks like a shortcut. Has a strong teaching instinct that occasionally becomes unsolicited instruction.

food.value: does not eat during darkroom sessions — professional habit from teaching; treats it as a clean workspace rule

activities.value: strongly prefers traditional darkroom printing over digital scanning — finds scanner output a compromise

social.value: dislikes the chat being used to share reference images or external work — believes it should only be for collective members' own work

domain_specific.value: shoots almost exclusively Kodak Tri-X and Ilford HP5 — sceptical of boutique and obscure film stocks

preference_history.old_value: dismissive of colour darkroom work — considers the process fussy and the results rarely worth it
preference_history.new_value: acknowledges colour darkroom printing as technically valid and sometimes compelling
preference_history.trigger: Yuki produced a series of colour darkroom prints that Otto called 'the most controlled colour work I have seen from this group' during critique

speaking_quirks: prefaces corrections with 'the thing people miss about this is...'
uses 'in my experience' before any opinion he wants to carry weight
refers to film stocks by their full technical name ('Kodak Tri-X 400' not just 'Tri-X')

personas.background: Shoots film as a deliberate counterweight to their digital design work. Very aesthetically precise — spends more time looking at a scene than shooting it. Joined the collective two years ago via a gallery opening where they met Nora. Their work is methodical and tends to divide the group.

food.value: brings their own tea to every session in a thermos — politely declines everything else without explaining

activities.value: very deliberate shooter — caps themselves at one or two rolls per session; becomes visibly uncomfortable watching rapid spray-and-pray shooting

social.value: prefers written critique over verbal group discussion — always submits notes after sessions rather than speaking live

domain_specific.value: aesthetic focus on grain structure — deliberately chooses high ISO films for the texture rather than despite it

preference_history.old_value: shoots exclusively in black and white — treats colour as aesthetically imprecise
preference_history.new_value: has begun experimenting with colour negative film for selected projects
preference_history.trigger: Margot's recent colour roll during the street photography session surprised Yuki — they commented that the palette had a restraint they had not expected from colour work

speaking_quirks: refers to images by their geometric properties rather than subject ('the triangulation in the lower third is unresolved')
starts critique with 'my read on this is...' to frame it as interpretation rather than verdict
uses silence — often the last to respond in a thread, then gives the most considered reply

personas.background: Shoots film alongside fieldwork. Homebrews his own developer and DIYs camera repairs on a tight budget. Brought several newer members into the group including Sol. Resourceful and sometimes pushy about making the collective more DIY-oriented and less reliant on the commercial darkroom.

food.value: always asks if there's leftover food from previous sessions — never brings his own

activities.value: strongly prefers developing at home over the collective's darkroom — finds group darkroom sessions inefficient

social.value: brings guests without much warning — has introduced three new members this way, two of whom joined

domain_specific.value: budget-maximalist — always finds the cheapest effective option and advocates for it loudly, sometimes to others' frustration

preference_history.old_value: pushing for the collective to move away from the rented darkroom toward a fully self-organised model
preference_history.new_value: accepts that the collective space has irreplaceable social and logistical value
preference_history.trigger: a session he ran from his flat had poor turnout and multiple complaints about the cramped conditions; the following session in the darkroom had the highest attendance of the year

speaking_quirks: references cost per frame when evaluating any gear or process decision
uses 'genuinely' as an intensifier before opinions he feels are underappreciated ('genuinely the most underrated developer out there')
signs off with 'lmk' on any message that requires a response

personas.background: Shoots architectural and urban landscape film photography as a counterpoint to her digital work. Technically precise and compositionally rigorous. Joined the collective through a contact at Nora's gallery. Has a preference for large prints that sometimes creates friction over the collective's shared printing budget.

food.value: vegan — never announces it but declines non-vegan food at events with 'I'm fine, thank you'

activities.value: strongly prefers planned shoots with clear compositional goals over open exploratory sessions

social.value: prefers written asynchronous critique over live verbal discussion — submits responses after studying images at home

domain_specific.value: judges prints by size — finds small prints frustrating and tends to comment that 'it needs room to breathe'

preference_history.old_value: produces tightly controlled purely architectural frames with no human presence
preference_history.new_value: deliberately incorporating human figures to introduce scale and narrative
preference_history.trigger: a Fen documentary piece shown at session 4 made Priya comment that she had 'always thought of people as compositional interruptions' — she arrived at session 5 with a roll that featured figures throughout

speaking_quirks: describes images in architectural language ('the negative space is load-bearing here')
qualifies opinions with 'from a compositional standpoint'
sends a single message per topic with no follow-up unless directly asked

personas.background: The youngest member, brought in by Callum after a student exhibition. Shoots everything — 35mm, medium format, pinhole, phone, video. No aesthetic loyalty. Their work polarises the group. Has the highest energy and the lowest punctuality in the collective.

food.value: always arrives late and without food — has been known to take Bex's coffee without asking

activities.value: prefers completely unstructured experimental sessions with no assignment or brief — chafes at themed shoots

social.value: overshares process — posts half-developed ideas and behind-the-scenes images in the group chat constantly

domain_specific.value: no aesthetic loyalty to any format or process — switches between pinhole, 35mm, phone, and video within a single session

preference_history.old_value: produces highly abstract work that consistently confuses the group during critique
preference_history.new_value: includes a brief written statement with experimental work to give entry points for critique
preference_history.trigger: group critique in session 3 stalled entirely on one of Sol's pieces — Nora asked for context and Sol realised the gap; they arrived at session 4 with a handwritten note for each print

speaking_quirks: starts sentences mid-thought as if continuing a conversation ('anyway so the point is—')
uses 'lowkey' and 'highkey' interchangeably and incorrectly
tags multiple people in the same message to loop everyone into side conversations

personas.background: Retired two years ago and joined the collective after an evening darkroom workshop ran by Nora. Has been shooting street photography seriously since retirement. Old-school sensibility — her work is quiet, precise, and frequently the most cohesive in the group. Strong resistance to digital workflow as a matter of principle.

food.value: brings homemade baked goods to every session without exception — has never arrived empty-handed

activities.value: strictly street photography — grows uncomfortable when the group discusses staged or studio-controlled compositions

social.value: prefers in-person critique over chat-based image sharing — rarely responds to images posted digitally

domain_specific.value: resists the digital scanning workflow — only shares prints in person or by post; has never uploaded a scan to the group

preference_history.old_value: categorically refuses any digital workflow — considers scanning a betrayal of analogue process
preference_history.new_value: accepts scanning as valid for group circulation and online sharing, though does not practise it herself
preference_history.trigger: Nora explained that two members had been unable to attend sessions and scanning was the only way for them to participate in critique; Margot said 'I suppose that's different' and dropped the objection

speaking_quirks: refers to photographers by surname only ('a Cartier-Bresson move', 'very Vivian Maier')
uses 'I rather think' before opinions she considers underappreciated
responds to images posted in the chat with a single word of precise description ('Quiet.' or 'Busy.')

personas.background: Based locally but travels frequently for commissions. Sporadic collective presence — sometimes absent for two sessions running, then fully engaged for a run of weeks. Documentary and social photography focus. Brings a more politically grounded perspective to critique that others sometimes find confrontational.

food.value: sporadic attendance means she often misses food coordination — tends to arrive and improvise

activities.value: dislikes photography that has no social function or intent — finds purely aesthetic work uninteresting to critique

social.value: drops into chat threads late, catches up quickly, and makes a point without much preamble

domain_specific.value: raises photographic ethics unprompted during critique — particularly around photographing vulnerable or unaware subjects

preference_history.old_value: works exclusively solo — does not collaborate on projects
preference_history.new_value: pursuing a collaborative documentary project with Callum on a local housing story
preference_history.trigger: Callum pitched the housing story during session 3 and Fen said 'if you actually go through with it, I'm in' — he sent her a draft at the start of session 4 and she committed

speaking_quirks: opens critique with 'what's the image asking of the viewer?' as a framing question
references field context unprompted ('I was shooting in Marseille last month and...')
uses 'arguably' before any point she expects pushback on

edges.history_summary: Both have been central to the collective from the beginning. Deep mutual respect for each other's technical knowledge but recurring tension around openness to new approaches — Nora is more inclusive, Otto more conservative. Disagreements surface during critique and in discussions about what counts as valid collective work.
shared_events: three years of joint session planning

edges.history_summary: Nora brought Bex in after an open workshop and has guided her development. Bex is one of the few members Nora gives one-on-one feedback to outside sessions. Nora finds Bex's enthusiasm a counterweight to some of the group's more entrenched attitudes.
shared_events: open workshop where Bex first appeared

edges.history_summary: Met at a gallery opening two years ago. Share an appreciation for deliberate, considered work. Rarely disagree in critique but operate in different registers — Yuki is more formal and withdrawn, Nora warmer and more facilitative.

Bond over a shared commitment to traditional process. Otto was the first to praise Margot's prints publicly in a session and she has respected him since. They are the most resistant pair when digital workflow or experimental approaches come up.
shared_events: shared resistance to scanning workflow thread

edges.history_summary: Mutual enthusiasm for experimental work. Bex admires Sol's fearlessness and Sol appreciates that Bex hypes their work without reservation. The most active pair in the chat between sessions.

Share technical rigour and a preference for deliberate composition. Disagree on subject matter — Yuki prefers texture and abstraction, Priya prefers structure and form — but find each other's critique useful.
shared_events: shared critique of each other's architecture series

edges.history_summary: Started a collaborative housing documentary project after session 3. Callum pitched it; Fen committed when she saw he was serious. Early stages are tense around methodology but both want it to work.

edges.relationship_type: introducer and introduced — now occasionally at odds
edges.history_summary: Callum brought Sol into the group. Initially supportive but Callum has grown frustrated with Sol's unreliability and finds their work increasingly inaccessible. Still friendly but the dynamic has shifted.
Both shoot documentary and people-focused work but have rarely engaged directly. Margot's quietness and Fen's sporadic presence means they have crossed paths at sessions without forming a connection.
shared_events: one shared critique of a documentary roll

edges.history_summary: Rarely address each other directly. Otto's verbose teaching style and Priya's preference for concise written critique mean their contributions rarely interact. Mutual respect without connection.
shared_events: group critique of Priya's architectural series

edges.history_summary: Yuki's precision and Sol's chaos sit at opposite ends of the collective's approach spectrum. They do not argue but Yuki's written critiques of Sol's work tend toward diplomatic bafflement. Sol respects Yuki's eye without understanding their process.

Both value intentionality in photography. Fen's ethical framing and Nora's methodological care put them on the same side of most collective debates. Nora often calls on Fen's perspective when she's present.
shared_events: joint planning of documentary-focused shoot brief

edges.history_summary: Both appreciate low-cost experimental approaches. Callum supplies Bex with homebrew developer occasionally. Bex enthusiastically promotes Callum's DIY tips to the group even when others are not interested.

group_norms.norm_text: Images shared in the group chat should be your own work — save reference images and inspiration links for in-session discussion
Critique should be constructive — lead with what the image achieves before suggesting alternatives
Sessions start at the agreed time — the group will not hold more than ten minutes for latecomers
